library(ggplot2)

# Exercise 1: Piecewise function in R

```{r}
xx <- seq(-3, 5, length.out = 100)

# Boolean masking: multiply each piece by TRUE/FALSE (1/0)
piece1 <-  0          * (xx < 0)
piece2 <- -2*xx       * (xx >= 0 & xx < 3)
piece3 <-  xx^3 / 10  * (xx >= 3)

y <- piece1 + piece2 + piece3

ggplot(data.frame(x = xx, y = y), aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)", title = "A piecewise function")
```

# Exercise 2: Draw separate lines for each piece

```{r}
df <- data.frame(x = xx, y = y) |>
  mutate(piece = case_when(
    xx < 0            ~ "0  (x < 0)",
    xx >= 0 & xx < 3  ~ "-2x  (0 \u2264 x < 3)",
    xx >= 3           ~ "x\u00b3/10  (x \u2265 3)"
  ))

ggplot(df, aes(x, y, color = piece)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)",
       title = "Piecewise function — pieces coloured separately",
       color = "Piece")
```

# Exercise 3: Piecewise function using `case_when()` (the SymPy.Piecewise equivalent)

In Python, `sympy.Piecewise()` defines a function with explicit conditions.
`dplyr::case_when()` is the idiomatic R equivalent.

```{r}
xx <- seq(-3, 5, length.out = 500)

fx <- case_when(
  xx < 0            ~  0,
  xx >= 0 & xx < 3  ~ -2 * xx,
  xx >= 3           ~  xx^3 / 10
)

ggplot(data.frame(x = xx, y = fx), aes(x, y)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.5) +
  labs(x = "x", y = "y = f(x)",
       title = "Piecewise function via case_when()")
```

```{r}
# Evaluate the piecewise function at a specific point, e.g. x = 1.5
x0  <- 1.5
fx0 <- case_when(x0 < 0 ~ 0, x0 >= 0 & x0 < 3 ~ -2*x0, x0 >= 3 ~ x0^3/10)
cat("f(1.5) =", fx0, "\n")
```
